## TL;DR

Extended `classifyAgentFailure` with **out-of-credit** and broader **quota/rate** patterns, and changed `formatAgentFailure` so every failure gets a one-line summary plus a `(CLI: …)` disclosure tail instead of leaking multi-line or JSON blobs into the UI. Added `agent-last-runs` filtering (14-day window, configured agents only, routing one-shots in the expanded list) and a **Show older and other runs** toggle on the Default agents tab. Table-driven tests cover real DeepInfra and Antigravity strings from production.

## Work and rationale

The #1098 pipeline already split formatted failures into summary vs raw via `splitAgentFailureDetail`, but `classifyAgentFailure` only matched auth, model, usage-limit (narrow wording), and network. DeepInfra’s “You need positive balance” and Antigravity’s `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` / 429 JSON never matched, so `formatAgentFailure` returned the entire stored string as the summary. That same path feeds task cards, the drawer, notifications, crash recovery, and `GET /api/agents/last-runs`.

Classification now runs on stripped ANSI text. **Out-of-credit** covers balance, insufficient credit, payment required, and HTTP 402. **Usage-limit** regex adds `Individual quota reached`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, and `429`, with timing copied from either `until HH:MM` (legacy “usage limit reached” copy) or `Resets in …` for provider cooldowns. The Copilot Auto tier branch is unchanged.

For anything still unclassified, **generic fallback** logic picks a short first line only when the message is single-line or not JSON-heavy across lines; otherwise it uses “<CLI> exited with an error.” Fix line is always “Open Raw CLI error for details.” Raw tail is ANSI-stripped and capped at 8k characters so disclosures stay bounded. Known failures keep their specific fix sentences; all paths use the same `(CLI: …)` marker so existing disclosure UI keeps working without migration.

Last-runs clutter came from `getAgentLastRuns` returning one row per distinct `agent` name in sessions history, including deleted roles, month-old built-in scans, and model-routing one-shots. Filtering lives in `src/core/agent-last-runs.ts` so vitest can cover it without mounting the view. Primary rows: agent name in configured role list or built-in config keys, started within 14 days, and not matching `Model router (` / `Decision check (`. The Agents page computes configured names from `localAgents` plus `config.data.builtInAgents` keys (with a static built-in id fallback). Hidden count drives the toggle; expanding shows all rows in API order so routing failures remain discoverable but not mixed into “current default agent problems.”

Docs: one paragraph in `user-docs/agents.md` under Agent failure messages.

## Approaches tried

Centralizing filter logic in core rather than SQL or API changes keeps read-time formatting (#1098 design) and avoids migrating stored `errorReason` strings. Server `/api/agents/last-runs` still returns the full set; the UI alone narrows display so preview boards without session history still render.

Reused `stripAnsi` from `close-out-failure.ts` instead of a third copy. Left LIMIT as one class with two summary templates so existing “usage limit reached until 14:00” expectations stay stable while new quota strings get clearer “hit a provider quota or rate limit” wording.

## Challenges and blockers

None on product logic. Verification depends on `repoos check --changed main` completing under server queue pressure; unit tests for classifier and filter pass locally in isolation.

## Key learnings

Failure text that embeds JSON on its own line must not become the card summary even when the first line looks innocent — multi-line opaque output should fall back to CLI name. Routing agents use human-readable session names (`Model router (openrouter)`); prefix matching is enough to exclude them from the default last-runs panel without maintaining an allowlist of provider ids.
